corpus.name: outline
corpus.why: Outline wiki: a large single-package TypeScript application (about 2,200 .ts/.tsx files) with a React client, a Koa server, path aliases (~, @server, @shared) and a plugin directory. It exercises app-style dead code where nothing is a published API.

corpus.name: typeorm
corpus.why: TypeORM: a widely used ORM library (pnpm monorepo, about 3,600 .ts files) whose public API is published from packages/typeorm/src/index.ts through a build directory (publishConfig.directory). It tests whether a library's public exports are mistaken for dead code.

corpus.name: ripgrep
corpus.why: ripgrep: a well-known Cargo workspace of ten library crates plus the rg binary crate. It mixes bin-crate code (where rustc flags unused pub items) with library crates that re-export through lib.rs. Benches are not checked: globset's bench target needs nightly `#![feature(test)]`.

corpus.name: axum
corpus.why: axum: the tokio web framework. Its handlers, extractors and responses are built from blanket trait impls, impls generated by macro_rules (all_the_tuples!), and a proc-macro crate, which is the hardest case for call-based reachability.

corpus.name: soft-serve
corpus.why: Charm's soft-serve: an actively maintained single Go module (git server over SSH/HTTP) with interfaces, a cmd/ tree and internal packages. Reused from benchmarks/inspect-field-audit/repos.json.

corpus.name: fastapi
corpus.why: FastAPI: a widely used, typed Python package. Reused from benchmarks/inspect-field-audit/repos.json, where it was the Python case.
